Name: Kamikochi
Description: Nature / Hiking (Japanese Alps) – Highland valley in the Northern Japan Alps; accessible via bus from Matsumoto or Takayama

Name: Narai-juku (Narai Post Town)
Description: Nagano Prefecture (Kiso Valley) – Town / Historic post town – Well‑preserved Edo‑period post town along the Nakasendo, known for its traditional wooden buildings

Name: Togakushi Shrine
Description: Complex of five shrines nestled in forested mountains, famous for its long avenue of cedar trees and zigzag path

Name: Jigokudani Monkey Park
Description: Wildlife / Snow monkeys – Famous for wild Japanese macaques bathing in hot springs during winter

Name: Monet's Pond
Description: Village pond (Monroe no Ike) whose clear turquoise water mirrors the sky — a real-life 'Monet's Pond', scenic and free. Best in summer/autumn.

Name: Kegon-ji Temple
Description: Historic temple known for its beautiful garden and seasonal flowers

Name: Shirakawa-go
Description: Village / UNESCO site – UNESCO World Heritage site featuring traditional gassho‑zukuri farmhouses

Name: Taki Shrine
Description: Scenic shrine, breathtaking otherworld setting (in Gifu). From 'otherworld Japan' video.

Name: Katsura Rikyu
Description: Palace / Garden – Imperial villa and garden in western Kyoto, renowned for its traditional architecture and landscape design

Name: Arashiyama Bamboo Forest
Description: Kyoto's iconic bamboo grove; free entry, best early morning. Real talk (Kyoto guide Naoya, 09-05): it looks stunning in photos but the actual walk is SHORT and way too crowded — low ROI. Consider Philosopher's Path (recommended) or Kibune instead.

Name: Philosopher's Path
Description: Kyoto canal-side walk; RECOMMENDED by guide Naoya — beautiful residential views esp. cherry-blossom and autumn seasons; great photos. (from 09-05 guide verdicts)

Name: Kibune
Description: Mountain village north of Kyoto; RECOMMENDED by guide Naoya — a bit far from the city but the best nature of Kyoto, cooler seasons (kawadoko river dining). (from 09-05 guide verdicts)

Name: Eikando Temple
Description: Kyoto autumn spot #1 (guide Naoya): famous autumn foliage + night illumination/light show, very popular with locals. Trip is Oct — check foliage timing.

Name: Tofukuji Temple
Description: Kyoto autumn spot #2 (guide Naoya): spectacular autumn leaves over Tsutenkyo bridge; often compared to Fushimi Inari crowds but this is THE autumn-view temple.

Name: Rurikoin Temple
Description: Kyoto autumn spot #3 (guide Naoya): autumn maple reflections on the polished table inside — REQUIRES reservation, limited entry.

Name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
Description: Iconic shrine with thousands of torii gates. Naoya's one-day route: GO 6-7am to beat the crowds (earlier he flagged it as too crowded LATER in the day — timing is everything).

Name: Kiyomizu-dera
Description: UNESCO temple in Higashiyama. Naoya one-day route: beautiful, but crowded — visit via the Higashiyama/Ninenzaka photo route. Was flagged 'too crowded' but route says worth it early.

Name: Gion District
Description: Kyoto's famous geisha/maiko district (Hanamachi). Naoya one-day route stop.

Name: Nishiki Market
Description: Kyoto's downtown covered food market ('Kyoto's kitchen'), 400yr old. Naoya one-day route: great lunch stop.

Name: Nijo Castle
Description: UNESCO World Heritage castle, 400-year-old palace. Naoya one-day route: afternoon stop if energy remains.

Name: Pontocho Alley
Description: Atmospheric dining/drinks alley by the Kamo River. Naoya one-day route: dinner + drinks end-of-day; kawadoko riverside dining this season.

Name: Nene-no-Michi
Description: Scenic stone-paved path in Higashiyama, Kyoto (near Kiyomizu/Kodai-ji) with bamboo + lantern-lit atmosphere. Home of the summer Higashiyama Bamboo Light-Up (moon-viewing road) — but that light show runs JULY-AUG only, ended for our Oct trip. Street itself is lovely year-round.

Name: Shipporyuji Temple
Description: Hidden otherworld temple in the Osaka hills. From 'hidden wonderland' otherworld video.

Name: Hasedera Temple (Nagaya Temple)
Description: Temple – Also known as Hasedera, famous for its large wooden Kannon statue and beautiful gardens

Name: Hazonji Temple (Baoshan Temple)
Description: Temple – Known as Hazon‑ji, historic temple with beautiful autumn foliage

Name: Tsubasoka Temple
Description: Temple – Small temple in Nara known for its serene atmosphere

Name: Hannya-ji Temple
Description: Nara temple, flower-framed in cosmos season, quieter than the main temple crowds.

Name: Futai-ji Temple
Description: Nara temple, quiet old architecture and a pond garden.

Name: Takisaka no Michi
Description: Mossy stone trail through forest history near Nara; wear grip shoes.

Name: Soni Highland
Description: Wide pampas-grass hills and sunset views in Nara; check bus times.

Name: Mitarai Valley
Description: Clear river pools and gorge scenery in Nara.

Name: Asuka Stone Monuments
Description: Ancient carved stones in rural Nara landscape, 6th-century era.

Name: Nachi Falls
Description: Japan's tallest single-drop waterfall (133m) and largest of the 48 Nachi Falls — sacred to Hiro Shrine, which worships the waterfall as its deity. Crest 13m, basin 10m deep, ~1 ton water/sec. Free view area, small fee for closest deck. Misty/otherworldly on rainy days.

Name: Hiroshima
Description: Visit Peace Memorial Park, Museum, Atomic Bomb Dome

Name: Shinsho-ji Temple / Shinsho-ji Zen Museum and Gardens
Description: Temple / Garden / Museum – Zen temple with beautiful gardens and a modern museum showcasing tea ceremony artifacts

Name: Itsukushima Shrine (Miyajima)
Description: Shrine / Island – Iconic floating torii gate; explore Miyajima island, deer, and Mount Misen

Name: Tomonoura
Description: Hiroshima fishing village that inspired Ponyo's seaside town. Ghibli real-world spot.

Name: Akiyoshido Cave
Description: Cave / Natural site – One of Japan's largest limestone caves, part of Akiyoshidai Quasi‑National Park

Name: Fukuoka
Description: Hakata tonkotsu ramen birthplace (Ichiran/Ippudo); underrated city, fewer crowds + cheaper hotels than Tokyo/Kyoto/Osaka. From sponsored city-hype video.

Name: Takasumi Shrine
Description: Mystical shrine at ~800m on the slopes of Mt. Hiko, Fukuoka — above-the-clouds scenery, magical in rain/mist. Featured in a DJI Pocket 4 cinematic video.

Name: Saga
Description: Prefecture / Region – Prefecture in Kyushu known for ceramics, hot springs, and rural landscapes

Name: Suginohara Ranch
Description: Ranch / Scenic spot – Ranch offering horseback riding and pastoral views; check exact location within Saga

Name: Okawachiyama
Description: Imari, Saga – Pottery village famous for Imari ware and traditional kilns

Name: Torii Sea / Uo Shrine Torii Gate
Description: Shrine / Coastal torii – Scenic torii gate standing in the sea, part of Uo Shrine (also called Ouo Shrine)

Name: Oita Ghibli Tunnel
Description: Tunnel / Scenic spot – Tunnel decorated with Studio Ghibli‑themed artwork, popular for photos and trains

Name: Kumanoza Shrine
Description: Shrine – Historic shrine in Kumamoto associated with Kumano faith, surrounded by forest

Name: Mizonokuchi Shrine / Mizonochi Cave
Description: Shrine / Cave – Cave shrine with stalactites; associated with water deities; scenic walking trails

Name: Cheonan Kawara / Amano Iwato Cave
Description: Cave / Mythological site – Amano Iwato (Heavenly Rock Cave) where Amaterasu hid; nearby Cheonan Kawara rock formations

Name: Takachino Gorge
Description: Gorge / Scenic spot – Verdant gorge with walking trails and waterfalls, popular for autumn colours

Name: Udo Shrine
Description: Shrine / Coastal cave – Unique shrine built inside a cave facing the ocean, dedicated to Yamasachihiko

Name: Amanoyasukawara (Amano Iwato area)
Description: Miyazaki Prefecture (Takachiho) – Mythological site / Plain – Sacred plain before Amano Iwato cave where the gods gathered to lure Amaterasu out

Name: Kagoshima
Description: Southern Kyushu city known for Sakurajima volcano, Satsuma cuisine, and historic sites like Sengan‑en

Name: Kirishima Shrine
Description: Shrine – Ancient shrine surrounded by forest and volcanic landscape, part of the Kirishima‑Yaku National Park

Name: Ogawa Falls
Description: Waterfall – Picturesque multi‑tiered waterfall in lush forest; great for hiking and photography

Name: Yakushima Island
Description: Island / Natural site – UNESCO World Heritage site known for ancient cedar forests, wildlife, and hiking trails; the cedar forests inspired Princess Mononoke. Ghibli real-world spot.

Name: Sensō-ji Temple
Description: Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple, famous for its Kaminarimon gate and Nakamise shopping street

Name: Imperial Palace
Description: Imperial residence, iconic Nijubashi double bridge

Name: Mandarake Nakano Broadway
Description: Nakano · vintage anime figure goldmine

Name: Mandarake Shibuya
Description: Shibuya Udagawacho · second-hand figures

Name: Anime-center Akihabara
Description: Akihabara · anime shopping/arcade

Name: Tokyo Tower
Description: Minato · landmark view

Name: Meiji Shrine
Description: Shibuya · shrine, forest path

Name: Ghibli Museum
Description: Mitaka · museum, advance reservation

Name: Seiseki-Sakuragaoka
Description: Tokyo hillside town (Tama) that inspired Whisper of the Heart. Ghibli real-world spot.

Name: Aogashima Island
Description: Remote volcanic island in the Izu chain; lush cliffs + turquoise water. Free to explore but need ferry/helicopter to reach. From 'Unreal places' slideshow.

Name: Shibuya Hikarie Sky Lobby
Description: Free 11F sky lobby 2 min from Shibuya station — huge-window view over Shibuya Crossing; great photos. Address: 2-21-1 Shibuya. Free Tokyo viewpoint (from Tokyo tour video).

Name: Tower Hall Funabori Observation Tower
Description: Free observation deck at 103m in Edogawa; hidden gem, no tourists — see Skytree, Tokyo Tower, Mt Fuji, whole city. Address: 4-1-1 Funabori. Free Tokyo viewpoint (from Tokyo tour video).

Name: Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center
Description: Free 8F observation terrace steps from Kaminarimon — view over Sensoji Temple + Tokyo Skytree. Address: 2-18-9 Kaminarimon, Taito. Free Tokyo viewpoint.

Name: Mount Fuji
Description: Early‑morning sunrise visit (JR Chūō Line → Fuji‑Kyūko Line)

Name: Asaba Ryokan
Description: Kawaguchiko – Accommodation (Ryokan) – Traditional ryokan with Lake Kawaguchiko views, on‑sen

Name: Lake Kawaguchi
Description: One of the best Mount Fuji view spots; free; beautiful in cherry-blossom and autumn seasons. From 'Unreal places' slideshow.

Name: Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen Shrine
Description: The main shrine of Mt. Fuji (north base, Fujiyoshida); traditional starting point of the Fuji climb. Featured in Fuji Soul Tours stopover itinerary.

Name: Shiraito Falls
Description: UNESCO World Heritage waterfall near Mt. Fuji (part of the Fuji listing); featured in Fuji Soul Tours stopover itinerary. Fuji area day stop.

Name: Kamakura
Description: Coastal temple town south of Tokyo — Great Buddha (Daibutsu), Hase-dera, Tsuruoka Hachimangu; on clear days Fuji rises over Sagami Bay from the beach. Free to wander (Daibutsu+Hase small fees). Easy ~1h day-trip from Tokyo.

Name: Enoshima Island
Description: Seaside island just down the coast from Kamakura — the classic spot for Fuji-over-the-bay views; sea caves, Enoshima Shrine, sunset coast. Pairs with a Kamakura day-trip.

Name: Chiba Prefecture
Description: Prefecture / Region – Prefecture east of Tokyo known for Tokyo Disney Resort, Narita Airport, and coastal scenery

Name: Sayama Hills
Description: Saitama wooded hills that inspired My Neighbor Totoro. Ghibli real-world spot.

Name: Hitachi Seaside Park
Description: Seasonal flower fields (blue nemophila hills); small entrance fee, best season varies. From 'Unreal places' slideshow.

Name: Kashima Jingu Shrine
Description: One of Japan's most important/oldest shrines — powerful otherworld atmosphere. From 'hidden wonderland' otherworld video.

Name: Kegon Falls
Description: Nikko (Tochigi) — the real view is from the lower deck: take the underground elevator down (tunnel walk + reveal are part of it); ~$4 cash only. Top free lookout is the lesser view. Day-trip from Tokyo via Tobu Nikko Line (book direct trains 2+ wks ahead).

Name: Nabana no Sato
Description: Flower park / Illumination – Famous for seasonal flower displays and winter illumination

Name: Sangi Railway
Description: Railway / Scenic line – Scenic local railway running through Mie, popular for autumn views

Name: Kumano Fireworks Festival
Description: Annual fireworks display over the Kumano River, held in summer (check dates)

Name: Sado Island
Description: Island / Cultural site – Known for its historic gold mines, traditional performing arts (Ondeko), and scenic coastline

Name: Eiheiji Temple
Description: Famous Soto Zen head temple in Fukui — forest setting. From 'hidden wonderland' otherworld video.

Name: Takaragawa Onsen Osenkaku
Description: Gunma riverside onsen (Minakami) — outdoor mixed rotenburo pools along a river in a misty forest; steam + traditional wooden buildings. From 'wake up to soft rain' onsen video.

Name: Oirase Gorge
Description: Scenic 14km stream valley from Lake Towada; free walking trail, lush forest and waterfalls. From 'Unreal places' slideshow.

Name: Sannobo Hie Shrine
Description: Hie/Hiyoshi shrine in Aomori — otherworld forest setting. From 'hidden wonderland' otherworld video.

Name: Yamadera Temple
Description: Temple – Also known as Risshaku‑ji, famous for its stone steps and panoramic mountain views

Name: Ginzan Onsen
Description: Charming traditional hot-spring town, magical in winter; walking free, baths have entrance fee. From 'Unreal places' slideshow.

Name: Tarumizu Ruins
Description: Hidden otherworldly ruins next to Yamadera — honeycomb rock + torii, ~15 min walk off the approach path. From 'otherworld Japan' video.

Name: Mount Yotel (Mount Yotei)
Description: Mountain / Volcanic – Also known as Mount Yotei, popular for skiing and autumn hiking; located near Niseko

Name: Taikodani Inari Shrine
Description: Shrine – Famous for its thousands of red torii gates leading up the mountainside

Name: Adachi Museum of Art
Description: Renowned for its Japanese garden and collection of modern Japanese paintings

Name: Tsuwano Street / Tsuwano Old Town
Description: Town / Historic district – Preserved Edo‑period atmosphere with traditional houses, sake breweries, and the Taikodani Inari approach

Name: Tottori Sand Dunes
Description: Natural landmark / Sand dunes – Japan's largest sand dunes, featuring camel rides, sand sculptures, and coastal views

Name: Nagoro Scarecrow Village
Description: Village known for its many life‑sized scarecrow dolls placed around the depopulated area

Name: Dogo Onsen
Description: Matsuyama, Ehime — oldest hot spring in Japan; inspired Spirited Away bathhouse. Ghibli real-world spot (off-mainland detour).
